Reproducing the benchmark

Source: vignettes/benchmark.Rmd
benchmark.Rmd

The package ships the full bench harness used in Jakel (2026): 14 of the FFTrees-bundled datasets × 20 stratified 70/30 splits × all runners.

Datasets 

library(adaptiveFFT)
FFT_DATASETS

One full run

The driver script lives at inst/bench/run_full_bench.R:

script <- system.file("bench", "run_full_bench.R", package = "adaptiveFFT")
file.show(script)
# source(script)   # ~3-4 hours on a single core

Output is appended to inst/bench/results/baseline_bench.fst as a long data.table:

dataset, seed_idx, runner, acc, bacc, f1, auc, frugality, train_time,
n_test, n_pos_test, notes

Pre-computed results

For convenience, the FST containing all 5,824 rows of the published bench is included at inst/bench/results/baseline_bench.fst:

res <- fst::read_fst(
  system.file("bench", "results", "baseline_bench.fst", package = "adaptiveFFT"))
str(res)

Headline numbers (paper Table 1) 

library(data.table)
dt <- as.data.table(res)
dt[seed_idx <= 20L,
   .(mean_bacc = round(mean(bacc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
     n         = .N),
   by = runner][order(-mean_bacc)]

Statistical tests

The dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank + rank-biserial effect-size analysis used in the paper is reproduced by inst/bench/make_stats.R:

source(system.file("bench", "make_stats.R", package = "adaptiveFFT"))
